title: Accessibility Fundamentals ♿
description: Learn about screen readers, focus management, and the basics of WCAG.

slides.title: What is Web Accessibility? 🌍
slides.content:
# Designing for Everyone

Accessibility (a11y) means making websites usable by people of all abilities, including those who rely on screen readers, keyboard navigation, or other assistive technologies.

It's not just an ethical choice – it's often a legal requirement and expands your audience. About 15% of the world's population has some form of disability.

slides.title: WCAG: The Guidelines 📜
slides.content:
# Web Content Accessibility Guidelines

WCAG is built on four principles (**POUR**):
- **Perceivable** – Users must be able to sense the content (e.g., alt text for images).
- **Operable** – Interface must be usable (keyboard navigation, no flashing content).
- **Understandable** – Content and controls must be clear.
- **Robust** – Compatible with current and future tools (clean HTML).

WCAG has conformance levels A, AA, AAA. Aim for AA.

quizData.question: What does 'a11y' stand for?

options.text: Accessibility (there are 11 letters between a and y)

quizData.explanation: a11y is a numeronym where 11 represents the omitted letters.

slides.title: Keyboard Navigation ⌨️
slides.content:
# Not Everyone Uses a Mouse

Many users navigate solely via keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space). Ensure:
- All interactive elements are reachable via Tab.
- Focus order is logical.
- There are no keyboard traps (places you can't tab out of).

By default, links, buttons, and form controls are focusable. Custom interactive widgets (made with `<div>`) need extra work to be keyboard accessible.

slides.title: Focus Management 🔦

quizData.question: It's acceptable to remove the focus outline if it doesn't match your design.
quizData.explanation: You must replace it with an equally clear focus indicator; removing it without replacement harms accessibility.

slides.title: Colour Contrast 🎨
slides.content:
# Text Must Be Readable

WCAG AA requires a contrast ratio of at least **4.5:1** for normal text and **3:1** for large text. Tools like WebAIM's Contrast Checker help you measure.

Don't rely on colour alone to convey information (e.g., "red items are required") – add text or icons as well.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Semantic HTML First

If you build with proper semantic elements, you'll already meet many accessibility criteria without extra effort. Accessibility starts with correct HTML.
